paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write a short essay on the use of robots. Try to imagine what will happen when more and more robots take the place of human beings in industry as well as people’s daily lives. You are required to write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，您有 30 分钟的时间写一篇有关机器人使用的短文。想象一下，当越来越多的机器人在工业和人们的日常生活中取代人类时，会发生什么。您需要写至少 150 字但不超过 200 字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Let’s say you love roller-skating. Just the thought of 26 on your roller-skates brings a smile to your face. You also know that roller-skating is excellent exercise. You have a 27 attitude toward it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 假设您喜欢轮滑。只要一想到穿上你的溜冰鞋，你的脸上就会露出笑容。您也知道轮滑是一项极好的运动。你对此有积极的态度。

paragraphs.sourceText: This description of roller-skating 28 the three components of an attitude: affect, cognition, and behavior. You love the activity; it’s great fun. These feelings 29 the affective or emotional component; they are an important ingredient in attitudes. The knowledge we have about the object constitutes the cognitive component of an attitude. You understand the health 30 that the activity can bring. Finally, attitudes have a behavioral component. Our attitudes 31 us to go outside to enjoy roller-skating.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对轮滑的描述说明了态度的三个组成部分：情感、认知和行为。你热爱这项活动；这很有趣。这些感受突出了情感或情感成分；它们是态度的重要组成部分。我们对物体的了解构成了态度的认知成分。您了解该活动可以带来的健康益处。最后，态度也包含行为成分。我们的态度促使我们出去享受轮滑。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, we don’t want to leave you with the 32 that these three components always work together 33 . They don’t; sometimes they clash. For example, let’s say you love pizza (affective component); however, you have high cholesterol and understand (knowledge component) that eating pizza may be bad for your health. Which behavior will your attitude result in, eating pizza or 34 it? The answer depends on which component happens to be stronger. If you are walking past a pizza restaurant at lunchtime, your emotions and feelings probably will be stronger than your knowledge that pizza may not be the best food for your health. In that instance, you have pizza for lunch. If you are at home trying to decide where to go for dinner, however, the knowledge component may 35 , and you decide to go where you can eat a healthier meal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，我们不想给您留下这三个组件总是完美配合的印象。他们不知道；有时他们会发生冲突。例如，假设您喜欢披萨（情感成分）；然而，您的胆固醇水平很高，并且了解（知识成分）吃披萨可能对您的健康有害。您的态度会导致哪种行为：吃披萨还是不吃披萨？答案取决于哪个成分恰好更强。如果您在午餐时间路过一家披萨店，您的情绪和感受可能会比您知道披萨可能不是对您的健康最好的食物更强烈。在这种情况下，你午餐吃披萨。然而，如果您在家中试图决定去哪里吃晚饭，那么知识部分可能会占上风，您会决定去哪里可以吃到更健康的饭菜。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Changing Generation
paragraphs.translationZh: 变化的一代

paragraphs.sourceText: A. It turns out today’s teenagers aren’t so scary after all. Results of USA WEEKEND’s Teens & Parents survey reveal a generation of young people who get along well with their parents and approve of the way they’re being raised. They think of their parents with affection and respect. They speak with Mom or Dad when they have a problem. Most feel that their parents understand them, and they believe their family is the No. 1 priority in their parents’ lives. Many even think their parents are cool! Although more than a third have an object in their rooms they would like to keep secret from their parents, rarely is it anything more alarming than a diary or off-color ( 低俗的) book or CD.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：事实证明，今天的青少年并没有那么可怕。 《美国周末》的青少年与家长调查结果显示，这一代年轻人与父母相处融洽，并认可他们的成长方式。他们怀着慈爱和尊敬的心情想起父母。当他们遇到问题时，他们会与妈妈或爸爸交谈。大多数人认为父母理解他们，并且相信家庭是父母生活中的第一要务。许多人甚至认为他们的父母很酷！尽管超过三分之一的人在房间里有一件物品，他们希望对父母保密，但很少有比日记、低俗书籍或 CD 更令人担忧的了。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. Such results may seem surprising against the background of shocking incidents that color the way the mass media portray the young. In October 2000, the same month the survey was taken, the Washington-based Center for Media and Public Affairs wrote in its publication Media Monitor that, in a recent month of TV news coverage of American youth, just 2% of teens were shown at home, and just 1% were portrayed in a work setting. In contrast, the criminal justice system accounted for nearly one out of every five visual backgrounds. No wonder parents worry their own kids might spin out of control once they hit the turbulent waters of adolescence.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 在大众媒体描绘年轻人的方式中发生的令人震惊的事件的背景下，这样的结果似乎令人惊讶。 2000 年 10 月，即进行调查的同月，总部位于华盛顿的媒体和公共事务中心在其出版物《媒体监测》中写道，在最近一个月的美国青少年电视新闻报道中，只有 2% 的青少年出现在家里​​，只有 1% 的青少年出现在工作环境中。相比之下，刑事司法系统几乎占五分之一的视觉背景。难怪父母担心自己的孩子一旦进入青春期的汹涌浪潮，可能会失去控制。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. The overall facts ought to reassure us. The survey shows us that today’s teens are affectionate, sensible and far happier than the angry and tortured souls that have been painted for us by stereotypes. From other sources, we also know teenage crime, drug abuse and premarital sex are in general decline. We, of course, need to pay attention to youngsters who are filled with discontent and hostility, but we should not allow these extreme cases to distort our view of most young people.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 总体事实应该让我们放心。调查显示，今天的青少年比刻板印象为我们描绘的愤怒和痛苦的灵魂更加深情、理智，而且快乐得多。从其他来源，我们还了解到青少年犯罪、吸毒和婚前性行为总体呈下降趋势。我们当然需要关注那些充满不满和敌意的青少年，但我们不应该让这些极端案例扭曲我们对大多数青少年的看法。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. My own research at the Stanford Center on Adolescence uses in-depth interviews with small samples of youngsters rather than large-scale survey. Still, in my studies and others I have read, I find the same patterns as in USA WEEKEND’S survey. Today’s teenagers admire their parents and welcome parental guidance about important matters such as career choice—though certainly not Mom and Dad’s advice on matters of personal taste, such as music or fashion. When we ask teens to choose a hero, they usually select an older family member rather than a remote public figure. Most teens say they enjoy the company of both parents and friends.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 我自己在斯坦福青少年中心的研究采用的是对青少年小样本的深入访谈，而不是大规模调查。尽管如此，在我的研究和我读过的其他文章中，我发现了与《美国周末》调查相同的模式。今天的青少年钦佩他们的父母，并欢迎父母在职业选择等重要问题上的指导——尽管肯定不是父母在音乐或时尚等个人品味问题上的建议。当我们要求青少年选择英雄时，他们通常会选择年长的家庭成员，而不是遥远的公众人物。大多数青少年表示他们喜欢父母和朋友的陪伴。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Contrary to some stereotypes, most adolescents believe they must be tolerant of differences among individuals (though they do not always find this easy in the cliquish ( 拉帮结派的) environment of high school). Many of them volunteer for community service with disadvantaged people. One prevalent quality we have found in teens’ statements about themselves, their friends and their families is a strikingly positive emotional tone. By and large, these are very nice kids, and as the band The Who used to sing, “The kids are alright.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 与一些刻板印象相反，大多数青少年认为他们必须容忍个体之间的差异（尽管他们在高中拉帮结派的环境中并不总是发现这很容易）。他们中的许多人自愿为弱势群体提供社区服务。我们在青少年关于自己、朋友和家人的陈述中发现了一个普遍的品质，那就是极其积极的情绪基调。总的来说，这些都是非常好的孩子，正如 The Who 乐队曾经唱的那样：“孩子们都很好。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F. How much is today’s spirit of harmony a change from our more turbulent past? A mere generation ago, parent-child relations were described as “the generation gap.” Yet even then reports of widespread youth rebellion were overdone: Most kids in the ’60s and ’70s shared their parents’ basic values. Still, it is true that American families are growing closer at the dawn of this new millennium ( 千年 ). Perhaps there is less to fight about, with the country in a period of tranquility and the dangers of drug abuse and other unwholesome behavior well known. Perhaps in the face of impersonal and intimidating globalization, a young person’s family feels more like a friendly haven than an oppressive trap. And perhaps parents are acting more like parents than in the recent past. Within just the past five years. I have noticed parents returning to a belief that teenagers need the guidance of elders rather than the liberal, “anything goes” mode of child-rearing that became popular in the second half of the 20th century.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 今天的和谐精神与我们更加动荡的过去相比有多大变化？就在一代人之前，亲子关系被描述为“代沟”。然而即便如此，有关青少年普遍叛逆的报道也有些言过其实：大多数 60 年代和 70 年代的孩子都认同父母的基本价值观。尽管如此，在新千年到来之际，美国家庭的关系确实变得更加紧密。也许没什么可争论的，因为这个国家正处于安宁时期，吸毒和其他不健康行为的危险众所周知。也许面对非人性化和令人生畏的全球化，年轻人的家庭感觉更像是一个友好的避风港，而不是一个压迫性的陷阱。也许父母的行为比最近更像父母了。短短五年内。我注意到父母们又重新认识到青少年需要长辈的指导，而不是20世纪下半叶流行的自由主义、“一切皆有可能”的育儿模式。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. But missing from all these data is the sense that today’s young care very much about their country, about the broader civic and political environment, or about the future of their society. They seem to be turning inward— generally in a pro-social manner, certainly with positive benefits for intimate relationships, but too often at the expense of a connection with the present and future world beyond, including the society they will one day inherit.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 但所有这些数据都忽略了这样一种感觉：今天的年轻人非常关心他们的国家，关心更广泛的公民和政治环境，或者他们社会的未来。他们似乎正在转向内向——通常以一种亲社会的方式，这当然会给亲密关系带来积极的好处，但往往是以牺牲与当前和未来世界的联系为代价的，包括他们有一天将继承的社会。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. Recently, we examined more than 400 essays on the “laws of life” that teens from two communities had written as part of an educational program initiated by the John Templeton Foundation in Radnor, Pa. In those essays, and in follow-up interviews with a few of the teenagers, we found lots of insight, positive feeling and inspirational thinking. But we also found little interest in civic life beyond the tight circles of their family and immediate friends.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 最近，我们审查了来自两个社区的青少年撰写的 400 多篇关于“生命法则”的文章，这些文章是宾夕法尼亚州拉德诺约翰邓普顿基金会发起的教育计划的一部分。在这些文章以及对一些青少年的后续采访中，我们发现了许多见解、积极的感觉和鼓舞人心的想法。但我们也发现，除了家人和直系朋友的小圈子之外，他们对公民生活没什么兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. For example, only one boy said he would like to be president when he grows up. When I was in high school, dozens in my class alone would have answered differently. In fact, other recent studies have found there has never been a time in American history when so small a proportion of young people have sought or accepted leadership roles in local civic organizations. It is also troubling that voting rates among our youngest eligible voters—18- to 24-year-olds—are way down: Little more than one in four now go to the polls, even in national elections, compared with almost twice that many when 18-year-olds were first given the vote.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一、例如，只有一个男孩说他长大后想当总统。当我上高中时，仅我班上的几十个人就会有不同的答案。事实上，最近的其他研究发现，在美国历史上，从未有过如此少比例的年轻人在当地公民组织中寻求或接受领导角色的情况。同样令人不安的是，我们最年轻的合格选民（18 至 24 岁）的投票率大幅下降：即使在全国选举中，现在也只有不到四分之一的人去投票，而 18 岁的年轻人第一次投票时，这一比例几乎是两倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. In our interviews, many students viewed politics with suspicion and distaste. “Most politicians are kind of crooked ( 不诚实的),” one student declared. Another, discussing national politics, said, “I feel like one person can’t do that much, and I get the impression most people don’t think a group of people can do that much.” Asked what they would like to change in the world, the students mentioned only personal concerns such as slowing down the pace of life, gaining good friends, becoming more spiritual, becoming either more materially successful or less materially oriented (depending on the student’s values), and being more respectful of the Earth, animals and other people. One boy said, “I’d rather be concentrating on artistic efforts than saving the world or something.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 在我们的采访中，许多学生对政治持怀疑和厌恶的态度。 “大多数政客都是不诚实的”，一名学生宣称。另一位在讨论国家政治时表示，“我觉得一个人做不到那么多，而且我的印象是大多数人都不认为一群人能做那么多。”当被问及他们想改变世界的什么时，学生们只提到了个人的担忧，例如放慢生活节奏，结交好朋友，变得更加精神，变得更加物质成功或更少物质导向（取决于学生的价值观），以及更加尊重地球、动物和其他人。一名男孩说：“我宁愿专注于艺术事业，也不愿专注于拯救世界之类的事情。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K. It is fine and healthy for teens to cultivate their personal interests, and it is good news when young people enjoy harmonious relations with their family and friends. But there is also a place in a young life for noble purposes that include a dedication to the broader society, a love of country and an aspiration to make their own leadership contributions.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 青少年培养个人兴趣是一件好事，也是健康的事情，与家人和朋友建立和谐的关系也是一个好消息。但年轻的生命中也有崇高的目标，包括对更广泛的社会的奉献、对国家的热爱以及为自己的领导贡献的渴望。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. In the past, the young have eagerly participated in national service and civic affairs, often with lots of energy and idealism. If this is not happening today, we should ask why. Our society needs the full participation of its younger citizens if it is to continue to thrive. We know the promise is there—this is a well-grounded, talented, warm-hearted group of youngsters. We have everything to gain by encouraging them to explore the world beyond their immediate experience and to prepare themselves for their turn at shaping that world.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 过去，年轻人热切地参与国家服务和公民事务，往往充满活力和理想主义。如果今天没有发生这种情况，我们应该问为什么。我们的社会要继续繁荣发展，就需要年轻公民的充分参与。我们知道前途就在那里——这是一群有基础、有才华、热心的年轻人。通过鼓励他们探索超越他们直接经验的世界，并为他们塑造这个世界做好准备，我们可以获得一切。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Not many young people eligible for voting are interested in local or national elections these days.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 如今，没有多少有资格投票的年轻人对地方或全国选举感兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Parents are concerned that their children may get involved in criminal offences once they reach their teens.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 家长担心他们的孩子一旦到了十几岁，可能会卷入刑事犯罪。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Even during the turbulent years of last century, youth rebellion was often exaggerated in the media.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 即使在上个世纪的动荡岁月里，青年的叛逆也经常被媒体夸大。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Teenagers of today often turn to their parents for advice on such important matters as career choice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 今天的青少年经常向父母寻求关于职业选择等重要问题的建议。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The incidence of teenage crime and misbehavior is decreasing nowadays.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 如今，青少年犯罪和不当行为的发生率正在下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Young people should have lofty ideals in life and strive to be leaders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41、青年人要有远大的人生理想，争做带头人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Some young people like to keep something to themselves and don’t want their parents to know about it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 有些年轻人喜欢把一些事情保密，不想让父母知道。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. It is beneficial to encourage young people to explore the broader world and get ready to make it a better place.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 鼓励年轻人探索更广阔的世界并为让世界变得更美好做好准备是有益的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Many teenagers now offer to render service to the needy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 现在许多青少年主动为有需要的人提供服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Interviews with students find many of them are only concerned about personal matters.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Manufactures of products that claim to be environmentally friendly will face tighter rules on how they are advertised to consumers under changes proposed by the Federal Trade Commission.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据联邦贸易委员会提议的改革，声称环保产品的制造商将面临更严格的向消费者广告方式的规定。

paragraphs.sourceText: The commission’s revised “Green Guides” warn marketers against using labels that make broad claims, like “eco- friendly.” Marketers must qualify their claims on the product packaging and limit them to a specific benefit, such as how much of the product is recycled.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该委员会修订后的“绿色指南”警告营销人员不要使用“环保”等宽泛主张的标签。营销人员必须对产品包装上的主张进行限定，并将其限制为特定的好处，例如产品的回收量。

paragraphs.sourceText: “This is really about trying to cut through the confusion that consumers have when they are buying a product and that businesses have when they are selling a product,” said Jon Leibowitz, chairman of the commission.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该委员会主席乔恩·莱博维茨 (Jon Leibowitz) 表示：“这实际上是为了消除消费者在购买产品时以及企业在销售产品时遇到的困惑。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The revisions come at a time when green marketing is on the rise. According to a new study, the number of 5 advertisements with green messages in mainstream magazines has risen since 1987, and peaked in 2008 at 10.4%. In 2009, the number dropped to 9%.
paragraphs.translationZh: 此次修订正值绿色营销兴起之际。一项新的研究显示，自1987年以来，主流杂志上出现的5个带有绿色信息的广告数量一直在上升，并在2008年达到峰值，达到10.4%。 2009年，这一数字下降至9%。

paragraphs.sourceText: But while the number of advertisements may have dipped, there has been a rapid spread of eco-labeling. There are both good and bad players in the eco-labeling game.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管广告数量可能有所下降，但生态标签却迅速普及。生态标签游戏中既有好玩家，也有坏玩家。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the last five years or so, there has been an explosion of green claims and environmental claims. It is clear that consumers don’t always know what they are getting.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在过去五年左右的时间里，绿色主张和环境主张激增。显然，消费者并不总是知道他们得到了什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: A handful of lawsuits have been filed in recent years against companies accused of using misleading environmental labels. In 2008 and 2009, class-action lawsuits ( 集体诉讼) were filed against SC Johnson for using “Greenlist” labels on its cleaning products. The lawsuits said that the label was misleading because it gave the impression that the products had been certified by a third party when the certification was the company’s own.
paragraphs.translationZh: 近年来，针对被指控使用误导性环境标签的公司提起了一些诉讼。 2008年和2009年，庄臣因在其清洁产品上使用“Greenlist”标签而被提起集体诉讼。诉讼称，该标签具有误导性，因为它给人的印象是产品已经过第三方认证，而实际上认证是公司自己的。

paragraphs.sourceText: “We are very proud of our accomplishments under the Greenlist system and we believe that we will prevail in these cases,” Christopher Beard, director of public affairs for SC Johnson, said, while acknowledging that “this has been an area that is difficult to navigate.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 庄臣公共事务总监克里斯托弗·比尔德 (Christopher Beard) 表示：“我们对绿名单体系下取得的成就感到非常自豪，我们相信我们将在这些情况下取得胜利。”他同时承认“这是一个难以驾驭的领域。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Companies have also taken it upon themselves to contest each other’s green claims.
paragraphs.translationZh: 各公司也开始对彼此的绿色主张提出质疑。

paragraphs.sourceText: David Mallen, associate director of the Council of Better Business Bureau, said in the last two years the organization had seen an increase in the number of claims companies were bringing against each other for false or misleading environmental product claims.
paragraphs.translationZh: 商业改善局委员会副主任大卫·马伦表示，过去两年，该组织发现各公司因虚假或误导性环境产品声明而相互提起的索赔数量有所增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: “About once a week, I have a client that will bring up a new certification I’ve never even heard of and I’m in this industry,” said Kevin Wilhelm, chief executive officer of Sustainable Business Consulting. “It’s kind of a Wild West, anybody can claim themselves to be green.” Mr. Wilhelm said the excess of labels made it difficult for businesses and consumers to know which labels they should pay attention to.
paragraphs.translationZh: “大约每周一次，我的一位客户会提出一项我从未听说过的新认证，而我就在这个行业，”可持续商业咨询公司首席执行官凯文·威廉 (Kevin Wilhelm) 说。 “这有点像狂野的西部，任何人都可以声称自己是绿色的。”威廉先生表示，过多的标签让企业和消费者很难知道他们应该注意哪些标签。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: America’s education system has become less a ladder of opportunity than a structure to transmit inequality from one generation to the next.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国的教育体系不再是一个机会的阶梯，而是一个将不平等从一代人传递到下一代的结构。

paragraphs.sourceText: That’s why school reform is so critical. This is an issue of equality, opportunity and national conscience. It’s not just about education, but about poverty and justice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是为什么学校改革如此重要。这是一个平等、机会和民族良知的问题。这不仅关系到教育，还关系到贫困和正义。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s true that the main reason inner-city schools do poorly isn’t teachers’ unions, but poverty. Southern states without strong teachers’ unions have schools at least as awful as those in union states. Some Chicago teachers seem to think that they shouldn’t be held accountable until poverty is solved. There’re steps we can take that would make some difference, and Mayor Rahm Emanuel is trying some of them—yet the union is resisting.
paragraphs.translationZh: 诚然，市中心学校表现不佳的主要原因不是教师工会，而是贫困。没有强大教师工会的南方各州的学校至少和工会州的学校一样糟糕。一些芝加哥教师似乎认为，在贫困问题得到解决之前，他们不应该承担责任。我们可以采取一些措施来带来一些改变，拉姆·伊曼纽尔市长正在尝试其中一些措施，但工会却在抵制。

paragraphs.sourceText: I’d be sympathetic if the union focused solely on higher compensation. Teachers need to be much better paid to attract the best college graduates to the nation’s worst schools. But, instead, the Chicago union seems to be using its political capital primarily to protect weak performers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果工会只关注更高的薪酬，我会表示同情。教师需要获得更高的薪酬才能吸引最优秀的大学毕业生到全国最差的学校就读。但相反，芝加哥工会似乎主要利用其政治资本来保护表现不佳的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: There’s solid evidence that there are huge differences in the effectiveness of teachers. The gold standard study by Harvard and Columbia University scholars found that even in high-poverty schools, teachers consistently had a huge positive or negative impact.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有确凿的证据表明，教师的效率存在巨大差异。哈佛大学和哥伦比亚大学学者的黄金标准研究发现，即使在高度贫困的学校，教师也始终会产生巨大的积极或消极影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: Get a bottom 1% teacher, and the effect is the same as if a child misses 40% of the school year. Get a teacher from the top 20%, and it’s as if a child has gone to school for an extra month or two. The study found that strong teachers in the fourth through eighth grades raised the skills of their students in ways that would last for decades. Just having a strong teacher for one elementary year left pupils a bit less likely to become mothers as teenagers, a bit more likely to go to college and earning more money at age 28.
paragraphs.translationZh: 找一位排名垫底 1% 的老师，其效果就如同一个孩子缺课了学年 40% 的时间一样。找一位来自前 20% 的老师，就好像孩子多上了一两个月的学。研究发现，四年级到八年级的优秀教师可以持续数十年地提高学生的技能。只要在小学一年里有一位优秀的老师，学生在青少年时期成为母亲的可能性就会降低一些，而在 28 岁时上大学并赚更多钱的可能性就会增加一些。

paragraphs.sourceText: How does one figure out who is a weak teacher? Yes, that’s a challenge. But researchers are improving systems to measure a teacher’s performance throughout the year, and, with three years of data, it’s usually possible to tell which teachers are failing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如何判断谁是弱老师？是的，这是一个挑战。但研究人员正在改进衡量教师全年表现的系统，并且通过三年的数据，通常可以判断哪些教师表现不佳。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately, the union in Chicago is insisting that teachers who are laid off—often for being ineffective—should get priority in new hiring. That’s an insult to students.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，芝加哥工会坚持认为，被解雇的教师（通常是因为效率低下）应该在新招聘中得到优先考虑。这是对学生的侮辱。

paragraphs.sourceText: Teaching is so important that it should be like other professions, with high pay and good working conditions but few job protections for bottom performers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 教学如此重要，以至于它应该像其他职业一样，拥有高薪和良好的工作条件，但对表现不佳的人几乎没有工作保护。

paragraphs.sourceText: This isn’t a battle between garment workers and greedy bosses. The central figures in the Chicago schools strike are neither strikers nor managers but 350,000 children. Protecting the union demand sacrifices those students, in effect turning a blind eye to the injustice in the education system.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这不是制衣工人和贪婪老板之间的战斗。芝加哥学校罢工的核心人物既不是罢工者，也不是管理者，而是35万名学生。保护工会的需求牺牲了这些学生，实际上对教育系统的不公正现象视而不见。

paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 我们对美国的教育体系了解多少？

paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 内城区学校表现不佳的主要原因是什么？

paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 笔者认为工会应该怎样做才能赢得民众的支持？

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. What is the finding of the gold standard study by Harvard and Columbia University scholars?
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 哈佛大学和哥伦比亚大学学者的黄金标准研究结果是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Why does the author say the Chicago union’s demand is an insult to students?
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 为什么作者说芝加哥工会的要求是对学生的侮辱？
